summary_en: Rasa Industries raised its dividend forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company increased full-year operating profit guidance by 19.4% to 7.4 billion yen due to strong semiconductor demand driven by AI and data center expansion, with high-purity phosphoric acid performing better than expected.
title_en: Notice of Revision to Consolidated Business Forecast for Second Quarter (Interim Period) and Full Year for Fiscal Year Ending March 2027, and Revision to Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
Rasa Industries announced a revision to its dividend forecast for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, based on upward revisions to its operating profit guidance. The company upgraded full-year operating profit from 6.2 billion yen to 7.4 billion yen, a 19.4% increase, and full-year net income attributable to parent company shareholders from 4.3 billion yen to 5.2 billion yen, a 20.9% increase. The interim period operating profit was also revised upward by 23.2%, reaching 3.45 billion yen.

The forecast revisions reflect stronger-than-expected performance across multiple business segments. In the specialty chemicals division, high-purity phosphoric acid for semiconductors performed well due to robust global semiconductor market conditions driven by widespread generative AI adoption and expanding data center investments. A high-purity phosphoric acid capacity expansion facility operated by the company's Taiwan subsidiary commenced operations in April 2026 and ramped up faster than anticipated. Sales of high-purity inorganic materials for compound semiconductors and gallium spot sales also contributed to results. The machinery division is expected to maintain guidance as originally provided, supported by strong construction machinery and electron beam welding processing orders.

The specific amount of the dividend increase was not disclosed in the announcement. The company had implemented a 5-for-1 stock split effective April 1, 2026, with earnings per share figures restated on a post-split basis for comparability.
